wifi: Network Connectivity Guide. Smart devices require a stable internet connection to function correctly. Most of our smart home hubs only support 2.4GHz Wi-Fi networks due to its better range through walls. If your router combines both 2.4GHz and 5GHz under one name, you might need to temporarily disable the 5GHz band during initial setup. To connect, open the mobile app, tap the add device icon, and enter your network password. Ensure your phone is connected to the same network before starting. If the device flashes a red LED, it means the password was incorrect or the signal is too weak. Moving the device closer to the router during setup often solves range issues. After successful pairing, the LED will turn solid green for five seconds and then turn off to save power. MAC filtering on your router must be turned off or updated with the device's MAC address, which is printed on the bottom sticker.
reset: Device Factory Reset Instructions. If your smart device becomes unresponsive or you wish to transfer ownership, a factory reset is necessary. Before proceeding, note that resetting will erase all custom schedules, user profiles, and network settings permanently. To initiate the reset, locate the small pinhole button on the back of the device. Using a paperclip or a similar tool, press and hold the button for exactly fifteen seconds while the device is plugged in. The status lights will rapidly flash amber to indicate the process has begun. Release the button and wait for two minutes while the internal memory is cleared and the firmware reboots. Once you hear a chime and see a slow pulsing blue light, the reset is complete. Do not unplug the power adapter during this process, as it may corrupt the operating system. After the reset, you must remove the device from your mobile app manually before it can be registered again.
camera: Security Camera Storage Options. Our indoor and outdoor security cameras offer two primary methods for saving recorded video footage. The standard method relies on an onboard MicroSD card slot. The cameras support cards up to two hundred and fifty-six gigabytes, formatted in FAT32. Local storage automatically overwrites the oldest clips when full. Alternatively, users can subscribe to our Secure Cloud service. The basic cloud tier retains motion events for seven days, while the premium tier offers thirty days of continuous twenty-four-hour recording. Cloud storage requires a minimum upload speed of two megabits per second to function reliably. If the internet connection drops, the camera will fall back to local storage if a card is present. Footage saved to the cloud is encrypted end-to-end and can be downloaded directly to your smartphone through the companion app. Video quality settings can be adjusted to save space, but higher resolutions will consume storage bandwidth much faster.
thermostat: Thermostat Climate Control Protocol. This document outlines how the smart thermostat regulates ambient temperature and interacts with HVAC systems. The device uses dual sensors to measure both temperature and humidity, adjusting output to optimize comfort. Users can configure a weekly schedule with up to four distinct periods per day: morning, away, evening, and sleep. The Eco mode override can be activated automatically using geofencing when the house is empty. Unlike traditional thermostats, this unit requires a C-wire for continuous power and will not function on batteries alone. If the display shows an E73 error, it indicates a power interruption from the furnace control board. Firmware updates are downloaded overnight between 2 AM and 4 AM to minimize disruptions. Compatibility extends to most 24V conventional and heat pump systems, but proprietary communicating systems will require a special adapter module installed by a certified technician.
lock: Smart Lock Mechanical and Digital Guide. The biometric smart lock provides keyless entry while retaining a physical override for safety. The motorized deadbolt is powered by four AA alkaline batteries, which typically last for eight to ten months under normal household usage. When battery life drops below twenty percent, the keypad will flash red and send a push notification. Lithium batteries are strictly prohibited because they may deliver a voltage spike that damages the mainboard. If the batteries die completely, a 9V battery can be held against the two terminals at the bottom of the exterior casing to provide temporary power. Up to fifty unique fingerprint profiles and one hundred numeric PIN codes can be stored simultaneously. The auto-lock feature secures the door automatically three minutes after it is closed, though this timer can be adjusted in the settings menu. A hidden mechanical keyhole is located behind the magnetic faceplate for emergencies.
